flawed_step: The claim that normality alone (with no T1 assumption) implies regularity. Without T1, points need not be closed, so normality cannot be applied to a point and a closed set.
counterexample: Sierpinski space X={0,1} with open sets ∅, {1}, X, so the closed sets are X, {0}, ∅. Normal: every pair of disjoint closed sets includes ∅, and (∅, C) is separated by the disjoint open sets ∅ and X. Not regular: take C={0} and x=1 not in C. The only open set containing 0 is X, which meets every open set containing 1.
assessment_summary: Without T1, normal does not imply regular. The Sierpinski space is trivially normal, since {0} and X are the only nonempty closed sets and they overlap, but the point 1 cannot be separated from the closed set {0}.
